content.comment_body: Hello, I'm working with a new [product_name] ([article_no]) with [version_no] and a [product_name] operator display. I continuously encounter issues with the TCP-IP connection between my PC ([product_name] software) and the [product_name]. When these issues arise, the [product_name] stops responding to pings and its network card disappears from the device list in the transfer page of the [product_name] software. I checked the IP address using the operator display: it is 192.168.0.3, with subnet mask 255.255.255.0 and gateway 192.168.0.0. I downloaded the program successfully at first, but now it is impossible to download further versions due to the communication problem. I have tried disabling the firewall, using different PCs, and swapping Ethernet cables, yet the issue persists. Is there a known bug in the [product_name] firmware [version_no]? Thank you in advance.
Can you share the IP address and subnet mask settings for your PC? Is there any router in the setup? Which version of the [product_name] software are you running?

Hello [user_name], the IP address set on my PC is 192.168.0.69, subnet mask is 255.255.255.0. There is no router in between. The Ethernet cable (not crossover) connects the PC directly to the second RJ45 port of the [product_name] operator display. My software version is [version_no].
In your situation, I suggest opening a support request. Alternatively, you might try upgrading the firmware to [version_no]. See [url]

Hello, your description suggests you may have interruptions in your Ethernet connection between the PC and the network. I've experienced something similar and often need to reconnect the cable frequently. Here are some tips: 1. Check all Ethernet cables to ensure they are firmly plugged in and connectors are not damaged. 2. Verify the power supply at the [product_name] operator display—if the power is unstable at the device where your PC connects, it can cause issues similar to Ethernet cable interruptions. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are facing unstable TCP-IP communication between [product_name] [version_no] and their PCs running [product_name] software, preventing reliable program downloads and resulting in device disconnections. The [product_name] becomes unresponsive to network commands and disappears from the software's device list, even after basic troubleshooting efforts such as cable swaps and firewall adjustments. This behavior may point to hardware, firmware, or power-related issues.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect dependable TCP-IP connectivity to enable smooth program downloads and updates via [product_name] software—without experiencing device disconnections or network interruptions.
